articles.title_zh: Houthis say at least 25 killed in Saudi air strike
facts_zh:
Houthis say at least 25 killed in Saudi air strike
- Published
Media linked to the Houthi movement in Yemen say that at least 25 people, including women and children, have been killed in airstrikes by Saudi Arabia.
There has been no comment from the Saudi-led coalition backing the internationally recognised government in Yemen.

Live video footage on Al Masirah - a television station run by the Houthis - has shown rescuers pulling bodies out of the rubble of several buildings in al-Shariyah, a town to the east of the capital, Sanaa.

Italy's Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani says he has been targeted by "cyber-criminals" who published his personal data online because of his country's support for Ukraine.
"For days now, cyber-criminals have been publishing my personal data on the dark web and seeking further information, effectively exposing me to new threats and intimidation," Tajani wrote on X.

articles.title_original: No clear winner after tight New Zealand general election
articles.title_zh: No clear winner after tight New Zealand general election
facts_zh:
No clear winner after tight New Zealand general election
- Published
There was no clear winner following New Zealand's election on Saturday, as the leaders of its two major parties preparing for negotiations to form a coalition government.

Prime Minister Christopher Luxon's centre-right National Party won 42 seats but was 19 short of the simple majority needed to form a government, despite being the largest party, preliminary results show.
Combined with their coalition partners ACT and New Zealand First, they would have a slim lead over the left-leaning bloc if a deal could be reached.

all_titles.en: No clear winner after tight New Zealand general election

articles.title_original: UK cannot 'cherry pick' EU single market deal, Barnier tells BBC
articles.title_zh: UK cannot 'cherry pick' EU single market deal, Barnier tells BBC
facts_zh:
UK cannot 'cherry pick' EU single market deal, Barnier tells BBC
- Published
The EU's former Brexit negotiator has warned that the UK cannot "cherry pick" which elements of the single market to which it subscribes, after Andy Burnham said he wanted to explore closer economic ties with Europe.
The prime minister has said rejoining the bloc's internal market was among options he could pursue as part of a reshaping of ties since the UK's exit from the EU nearly six years ago.
But Michel Barnier told the BBC's Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg that EU members would insist on the UK readopting certain conditions, such as the free movement of people, to gain access.

articles.title_original: Meghan's father Thomas Markle under house arrest after child sex abuse material charge
articles.title_zh: Meghan's father Thomas Markle under house arrest after child sex abuse material charge
facts_zh:
Meghan's father Thomas Markle under house arrest after child sex abuse material charge
- Published
Thomas Markle, the father of Meghan, Duchess of Sussex, has been placed under house detention at his assisted living facility in Florida after being charged over possession of child sex abuse material.
Markle, 82, was arrested in Florida on a federal complaint alleging he held images that show child sex abuse, the US Department of Justice (DoJ) said.
He is charged with one count of possessing indecent images of children, the DoJ said.

all_titles.en: Meghan's father Thomas Markle under house arrest after child sex abuse material charge

articles.title_original: Paraguay's president impeached and under house arrest after bank collapse
articles.title_zh: Paraguay's president impeached and under house arrest after bank collapse
facts_zh:
Paraguay's president impeached and under house arrest after bank collapse
- Published
Paraguay's President Santiago Peña has been impeached and placed under house arrest after a bank collapse triggered a crisis that left more than half of the country's population without access to their accounts.

Peña was arrested on Friday minutes after lawmakers, including from his own party, unanimously voted to remove him from office following the collapse earlier this week of Ueno Bank, which has links to his private business interests.
He had offered to step down on Thursday.

all_titles.en: Paraguay's president impeached and under house arrest after bank collapse

articles.title_original: Pope in 'pretty good health' as he starts Latin America tour
articles.title_zh: Pope in 'pretty good health' as he starts Latin America tour
facts_zh:
Pope in 'pretty good health' as he starts Latin America tour
- Published
Pope Leo XIV has told reporters travelling with him to Latin America he is "in pretty good health", in his first comments on his condition since having surgery for lung cancer.
The Pope has arrived in Uruguay, the first stop of a 12-day tour which he is undertaking only three weeks after his operation.
The pontiff, 71, also said he was "very happy" to be able to make the trip which was thrown into doubt last month when doctors discovered a tumour during a routine scan.

all_titles.en: Pope in 'pretty good health' as he starts Latin America tour
